newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India stocks drift awaiting policy plan.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India stocks drift awaiting policy plan.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts eased in mostly light trade on Tuesday as the market continued to ignore local stock market gains, traders said.
"The local market is getting excited ahead of the prime minister's speech, but foreign investors have not really been in," a trader said.

Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Monday he would announce new economic policy measures this week, with local market gains on Tuesday driven by rumours about a possible hike in the equity limit of foreign investment in State Bank of India (SBI).

The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed down 0.31 points at 69.25, with the premium over the local market at 9.67 percent, well down on Monday's 11.73 percent and from nearly 15 percent on Friday.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index closed 41.46 points higher at 3,604.20.
The trader said Indian GDR prices were likely to be led by Gowda's speech, and were unlikely to show major changes before.
State Bank of India and Reliance again attracted some volume, with both trading higher. SBI GDRs added 25 cents to $19.50/$20.50 and Reliance rose 30 cents to $14.35/$15.35.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 1.74 points up at 66.47, a premium of 53.98 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite index shed 1.85 points to a provisional 662.85.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended 0.65 points lower at 98.18, a premium of 5.49 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index lost 10.75 points to 7,146.21.
